results.principle: Issuing an invoice recognises revenue and creates a receivable of equal value.
Every posting is balanced. Debits equal credits, without exception.
With no discount, the invoice total is the agreed unit price times quantity.
Before any collection, the whole invoice is outstanding.
An unpaid submitted invoice is Unpaid, and Unpaid is a real state, not a default.
The document total is the sum of its lines. No line is silently dropped.
An offer is not a transaction. A quotation moves no money and no goods.
An accepted order is a promise, not a posting. Revenue is not recognised on order.
Ordering goods incurs no liability until they are received or billed.
An internal request is not a commitment to any third party.
An offer must state the same price the sale would use, or it is not an offer.
Paying an invoice in full leaves nothing outstanding.
A part payment reduces the receivable by exactly what was paid, no more.
An invoice paid in part is Partly Paid. It is neither open nor settled.
Collecting cash converts a receivable into cash. It does not create revenue.
You cannot collect more against an invoice than it is worth.

results.principle: Successive part payments settle an invoice exactly. Rounding never creates or destroys money.
A supplier bill creates a payable equal to the billed amount.
A purchase is valued at the purchase price, never the selling price.
Paying a supplier discharges the liability and reduces cash.
Part-paying a bill leaves the rest owed.
You cannot discharge more liability than exists.

The unit-of-measure conversion belongs to the item master. A caller may not assert it.

results.principle: Naming a tax template must apply that template's rates, or the document must be refused. It may not name an 18% template and carry no tax at all.
A tax row claiming to belong to an 18% template may not carry a 0% rate. Either the row matches the template it names, or the document is refused.

results.principle: A document that posts nothing owes nothing.
Submission is a real state change. A posted invoice is not a draft.
A draft has no effect on the ledger. Nothing is real until submitted.
A foreign-currency invoice must post to the ledger at the published rate for its posting date. The rate is a fact about the world, not a number the writer of the document gets to choose.
